result.instructions: Tools for Browserbase, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which of our browser sessions are still running, and how long have they been up?"; "Open this page in a cloud browser and give me its status code and content type."; "Search the web for recent articles about our product and list the top five results.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Browserbase data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run browserbase_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run browserbase_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run browserbase_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. browserbase_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: browserbase_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the Browserbase projects this API key can use, with their concurrency limits. Good first call to find a projectId. Browserbase API: GET /v1/projects.

tools.name: browserbase_get_project_usage
tools.title: Get project usage
tools.description: Get the usage figures for one project (sessions, browser time and proxy bytes, as the API returns them). Browserbase API: GET /v1/projects/{id}/usage.

tools.name: browserbase_list_sessions
tools.title: List sessions
tools.description: List browser sessions, newest first, with their status (RUNNING, COMPLETED, ERROR, TIMED_OUT, REQUEST_RELEASE), timing and metadata. Browserbase API: GET /v1/sessions.

status.description: Filter by status, e.g. RUNNING, COMPLETED, ERROR or TIMED_OUT.

tools.name: browserbase_get_session
tools.title: Get a session
tools.description: Get one browser session by id: status, region, start and end times, and its connection details. Browserbase API: GET /v1/sessions/{id}.

session_id.description: The session id (from browserbase_list_sessions or browserbase_create_session).

tools.name: browserbase_create_session
tools.title: Create a session
tools.description: Start a new cloud browser session and return its record. Starts billed browser time. Optionally keep the session open and reuse a saved context (cookies and logins). Browserbase API: POST /v1/sessions.

keep_alive.description: Keep the session alive after the client disconnects.

timeout_seconds.description: Session timeout in seconds, as the Browserbase API accepts it.

context_id.description: A saved context id to load into the browser.

context_persist.description: Save changes to the context when the session ends.

tools.name: browserbase_release_session
tools.title: Release a session
tools.description: Ask Browserbase to end a session and release its browser (status REQUEST_RELEASE). Stops billed browser time for that session. Browserbase API: POST /v1/sessions/{id}.

session_id.description: The session id (from browserbase_list_sessions or browserbase_create_session).

tools.name: browserbase_fetch_page
tools.title: Fetch a page
tools.description: Fetch one web page through Browserbase and return its status code, headers, content and content type. Browserbase API: POST /v1/fetch.

url.description: The full http or https URL to fetch.

allow_redirects.description: Follow HTTP redirects (default as the API decides).

tools.name: browserbase_web_search
tools.title: Search the web
tools.description: Search the web through Browserbase and return matching results with titles, URLs and excerpts. Browserbase API: POST /v1/search.

include_domains.description: Only return results from these domains.

exclude_domains.description: Leave out results from these domains.

prompts.name: getting_started
prompts.title: Get started with Browserbase
prompts.description: What you can do with Browserbase here, with example requests to try.
